verdicts.evidence: Removing the existsSync early return just routes an absent lock through readFileSync's ENOENT, which the surrounding try/catch already converts to the same `null`. Measured: byte-identical output across 30 lock fixtures (absent, malformed, empty, directory-as-lock, wrong version, bad corpus shapes), the CLI cycle and the shim.

verdicts.evidence: readFileSync with encoding "" returns a Buffer instead of a string, and JSON.parse coerces it through toString() to the same utf8 text. Measured: identical parse of a lock containing non-ASCII (writtenBy "é☃"), and byte-identical output over all 30 lock fixtures including the BOM and empty-file cases, the CLI cycle and the shim.

verdicts.evidence: `&&` to `||` accepts any truthy corpus value and, worse, makes a lock containing "corpus": null throw on j.corpus.name into the outer catch so the WHOLE lock reads as absent. Measured on the CLI: that mission flips from corpus status verifiable to unrecorded with strict conformance gaps 36 -> 37, and locks pinned {name:7} / "acme" / {} now surface a corpusDrift that does not exist.

verdicts.evidence: Reachable only through JSON.parse output, where no non-object value (string, number, boolean, array element, null) carries string `name` and `version` properties, so the typeof check can never be what rejects. Measured: byte-identical output over the 8 malformed-corpus lock fixtures (string, number, 0, false, array, empty object, numeric name, numeric version), the CLI cycle, the shim and the control; the same fixtures do change under mutants 33/35/36, so the site is demonstrably observed.

verdicts.evidence: A numeric corpus.name is accepted as a valid pin. Measured on the CLI with a lock pinned {name: 7, version: "1.0.0"} beside a runward/rules/corpus.json of {name: "acme", version: "1.0.0"}: corpusDrift goes from null to {"pinned":{"name":7,...},"onDisk":{...}}, reporting a corpus drift that the malformed-pin rule exists to suppress.
